summary.text: Mark Warner is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from Virginia, first elected in 2008 and previously Governor of Virginia from 2002 to 2006. Before politics he was a telecommunications entrepreneur who co-founded the company that became Nextel. He is running for re-election, citing work on infrastructure investment, domestic manufacturing, health care costs, and his role on the Senate Intelligence Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Indianapolis, Indiana, in 1954. According to his Senate office, he is the son of a Marine who fought at Iwo Jima, grew up in a family that moved often, and was the first person in his family to graduate from college.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from George Washington University (his Senate biography says he graduated as valedictorian) and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1980.
Worked as a staffer for Sen. Chris Dodd and served as chair of the Virginia Democratic Party.

Co-founded the company that became the wireless carrier Nextel. According to his Senate biography, he spent more than 20 years as a technology entrepreneur and investor in start-up technology companies, and launched philanthropic initiatives including the Virginia Health Care Foundation.
Won the 2001 race for Governor of Virginia and served from 2002 to 2006, governing with a Republican-majority legislature.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2008 and took office in 2009; Ballotpedia lists his current term as ending in 2027. He won re-election in 2014 and 2020 (defeating Republican Daniel Gade in 2020).

Serves as Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and is a member of the Senate Finance, Banking, Budget, and Rules and Administration committees; has chaired the Intelligence Committee earlier in his Senate tenure.
According to his Senate office, he is married to Lisa; they have three daughters and two grandsons.
